title: Ayodhya's Ram Temple to Be Lit With 1 Lakh Diyas for the 10th Deepotsav
excerpt: The Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Trust will light one lakh diyas inside the temple complex with about 1,000 volunteers in five zones, while the city separately targets 30 lakh diyas at Ram Ki Paidi.
body:
• Ayodhya's Ram temple will be illuminated with one lakh diyas during Deepotsav, the Uttar Pradesh government said.
  • Around 1,000 volunteers will help light the lamps across five zones inside the temple complex, the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust plan says.
  • Separately, the district administration targets 30 lakh diyas at Ram Ki Paidi and the Saryu ghats for the 10th Deepotsav, with the main lighting on November 7.
  • The temple trust has divided the complex into five zones, and preparations to implement the plan on the ground will be completed over the next five days.

Ayodhya's Ram temple will be lit up with one lakh diyas during Deepotsav, the Uttar Pradesh government has said. Around 1,000 volunteers will help light the lamps across five zones of the temple complex, according to Inshorts' report of the announcement.

The Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust has finalised the plan to light the diyas inside the temple complex using about 1,000 volunteers divided into five zones, with named zone leaders and assigned team responsibilities, according to Particle News' summary of the arrangements. The temple lighting will be carried out with operational support from the Uttar Pradesh Police and the Central Reserve Police Force to manage crowd and security.

Two lightings, two scales

The temple-complex lighting is distinct from the city's larger public effort. The district administration has set a separate target to light 30 lakh diyas at Ram Ki Paidi, on the banks of the Saryu, for the 10th edition of Deepotsav. That wider effort remains separate from the confirmed temple-complex arrangements.

For visitors, Ayodhya's municipal and district authorities have announced logistics including 471 bio-toilets, 85 water coolers, 25 water kiosks, deployable tankers, roughly 792 sanitation workers and a 55-vehicle waste fleet, according to Particle News.

The festival around it

Deepotsav is scheduled from November 5 to 7, with related events continuing on November 8, according to Amar Ujala's report of the chief minister's remarks. Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath said the 10th Deepotsav will showcase the city's cultural heritage and the development undertaken since 2017, pointing to the Ram temple, Maharishi Valmiki International Airport, the redeveloped Ram Path, renovated ghats and Ayodhya's development as a solar city.

The festival began in 2017 with the lighting of 1.71 lakh diyas and has grown since, the chief minister said. "Like every year, devotees of Lord Ram are ready to create a world record in diya-lighting this year as well," he said. The banks of the Saryu will carry tableaux depicting episodes from the Ramayana, processions and cultural performances alongside the lighting.

What it means locally

The diya orders are also an income event for the region's potters. Local potter families have reported large bulk orders and sharply higher festival incomes as demand surged, with electric wheels boosting production and village workshops supplying hundreds of thousands of lamps for this Deepotsav, Particle News reported.

Deepotsav, which began in 2017, marks Diwali in Ayodhya — the city tradition holds to be Lord Ram's home — with the main diya lighting at Ram Ki Paidi scheduled for November 7. Preparations inside the temple complex will be completed over the next five days, the government said.
